mean_curvature — 3D curvature op

• Data kinds: points → signal

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.mean_curvature(points, k=25, normals=None) (to call the implementation directly, import curvature3d; curvature3d.mean_curvature(points, k=25, normals=None); from the registry, ops3d.get("mean_curvature"))

Usage

Mean curvature H = (k1+k2)/2. → (N,). A quantity that depends on the orientation.

normals (oriented reference normals, (N,3)): when omitted, a convex-side heuristic is used (the concave/convex sign of an open surface is undefined). Passing oriented normals aligns with the global orientation and yields the correct sign.

Notes:

• The computation is the same as principal_curvatures (PCA normal of the k+1 neighbourhood + local quadric surface fit) and returns (k1 + k2) / 2. Units are 1/length.

• The sign follows the convention convex = positive, and corresponds to global concave/convex only when normals is passed. When omitted, H of an open surface is always on the convex side (equivalent to the absolute value).

• Points with fewer than 5 neighbours get 0. k is truncated to N-1.

• A sphere of radius R gives 1/R, a cylinder 1/(2R), a plane 0. A saddle point (k1 = -k2) also gives 0, but gaussian_curvature is negative there, so the two can be told apart.

• normals must be (N,3) with finite, non-zero rows (ValueError). Deterministic.
